hypothesis: Decoupling physical-residual prediction target from compensated tracking surface can distinguish whether coupled target coordinates cause physical tracking loss. Frozen-W0 fit ease is not the rationale.
only_changed_factor: Completed-interval prediction reference uses a_req on all axes; tracking surface remains clip(s-Ms*eta).
baseline: Frozen C5 Ms=My=110, same 12 physical scenes; reuse pinned B72 and C5 results.
launch_protocol: Prepare isolated code and cross-language/no-Plant checks; main-source review; at most one first flight; engineering/raw safety review; then remaining11. No automatic retry or extension.
physical_assumptions: Existing ideal state feedback; no true wind/configuration/Plant oracle deployment inputs.
scoring: 0-20s 3D position RMSE, unrounded values, 1e-12 m tolerance; existing safety and actuator checks.

screen_gates.failure_action: Close fixed candidate; no My/parameter/seed sweep, no DEV72 or TEST extension.

mechanism_reports: Prediction target and Ms/My identities on all update events.
Same-run physical u-d0, coordinated u-d0-Ms*rf, prediction residual, early/late and per-axis position error.
All scenes and all failures; no cross-controller different-state component causal claim.
scientific_limits: Ms!=My leaves a tracking-coordinate mismatch term; ideal fitting physical d0 does not prove Q improves.
Finite-path proof must explicitly retain (My-Ms)*rf if rewritten in tracking coordinates.
Success is an isolation result, not sufficient proof of new method originality.
No use of C5 TEST results to tune or select; any new final candidate needs a fresh sealed independent test.
